messages:
Slotera Support: hey team — we're seeing a big p95/p99 regression on our /v1/generate route starting ~2026-06-15T06:15Z. p99 jumped to ~3.2s from ~450ms. This started after the midnight batch deploy on our side but runs were steady before. Any quick checks we should do?

Alex G: thanks — can you paste a couple request ids and the time window? also which model + config (streaming on/off, max_tokens, temperature)?

Slotera Support: request ids: rQn-58z, rQn-60b, rQn-61l in window 06:13-06:19Z. Using redwood/model-xl-32k, streaming=false, max_tokens=12000 (we do long-completion workflows).

Priya S: noted. tagging eng-sre and runtime. Priya running quick trace search for those request ids...

deploy-bot: trace-search job started for ids [rQn-58z,rQn-60b,rQn-61l] (job 9832).

Priya S: initial traces show those requests had a lot of KV cache misses and backend exec spikes at the tail. CPU on the serving pods climbed and we saw queuing on the per-tenant token throttler. p50 fine, but p95/p99 dominated by a small subset of requests that had very large decode lengths.

Ben T: interesting — slotera-prod has a config that allows very large requests w/out routing to a dedicated pool right? I recall a custom allowlist they added last quarter to let big-jobs through to shared pools. Could be noisy neighbor effects (large token blowouts + cache thrash).

Maria L: can you confirm whether per-tenant throttles kicked in or whether it was the global autoscaler? logs show multiple "throttle: tenant_token_window_exceeded" lines around 06:16Z for slotera-prod.

Priya S: confirmed. snippets from logs: 
```
[06:16:12Z] tenant=slotera-prod request_id=rQn-58z throttle_type=token_window result=throttled window_ms=1000 tokens=15234 limit=10000
[06:16:12Z] tenant=slotera-prod serving_pod=gw-12 cpu=92% kv_cache_miss=true
```

Alex G: ok that matches noisy neighbor + per-tenant token throttle. two paths: 1) short-term mitigation = put slotera-prod on temporary dedicated pool or increase their per-tenant limit, and create an allowlist to route very long requests to a separate capacity; 2) medium-term = enforce per-request token caps and fast-fail/circuit-breaker for extreme token counts.

Slotera Support: we can accept routing long jobs to a private pool, but need guidance on config changes. We want minimal disruption to our jobs.

Ben T: Proposed quick mitigation we can flip in <10m: add a routing rule that sends requests with max_tokens > 8k OR estimated_output_tokens > 8k to a dedicated burst pool (slotera-burst). Fallback: if slotera-burst is saturated, return 429 with a helpful payload. Patch looks like: 
```yaml
routing_rules:
  - name: slotera-long-run-routing
    match:
      tenant: slotera-prod
      or:
        - request.header.x-estimated-output-tokens > 8000
        - request.body.max_tokens > 8000
    action:
      route_to: slotera-burst-pool
      fallback: return_429
      metrics: tag=slotera_long_route
```

Maria L: also recommend enabling per-tenant short-circuit for high token requests: set per_request_token_limit=16k and enable fast_fail=true. That prevents cache thrash from single monstrous requests.

Priya S: I'll roll both configs to staging then prod. Maria do you want to adjust throttler windows (currently 1s)? increasing window can smooth but may hide spikes. I'd rather route than blur limits.

Maria L: agreed. route + fast_fail. keep throttler windows as-is.

deploy-bot: deploying routing policy slotera-long-run-routing -> canary -> 3 pods.

ops-bot: alert suppressed for slotera-prod during maintenance window (30m).

Alex G: while that deploy goes, we can also shadow smaller model variant to see QPS impact: shadow route to model-xl-quant-8bit. If tail is from kernel latency, smaller model might reduce cost and tail latency.

Slotera Support: thanks — please keep us posted and we'll pause our large batch for 20 minutes to avoid thrashing the burst pool.

deploy-bot: canary deployment complete (3 pods). routing rule active for 12s.

Priya S: early metrics — p99 for slotera /v1/generate dropped from 3.2s -> 720ms after rule applied, error rate stable. Some 429s logged for requests with max_tokens > 8k (expected).

Ben T: good. I'll open a follow-up for Dedicated capacity proposal (cost + SLA) so slotera can move long-jobs to reserved pool. For now we leave the routing rule enabled and tag their account for review.

Slotera Support: confirmed reduced latency on our side. we see the 429s and will rework some batch jobs. thanks for the quick help :raised_hands:

Maria L: next steps for internal: 1) document ephemeral routing policy pattern for long-token workloads; 2) add a diagnostics trace tag to better attribute cache-thrash (tenant_token_footprint); 3) propose per-tenant billing/limits guardrail for long-run requests.

Alex G: adding those to tech debt board. closing this thread once we get a final postmortem doc from eng-sre with timeline.

Slotera Support: appreciated. we'll follow up on Dedicated capacity request via the account rep.

Maria L: marking incident resolved — will attach traces and metric charts to the follow-up PM.

Priya S: final last point — create a customer-facing KB entry for "Large token workloads causing p99 regressions" with recommended routing and config snippets. I'll draft it.

Slotera Support: thanks again!
